summary: P3 из ревью T-0756 (finding N1, re-surfaced as N2 in T-0723's nits): isInstanceParticipant/isInstanceParticipantBatch (src/http/process-projection.ts) clause (1) — the audit-actor match — was never ACTOR_ACTIVE-gated, unlike clause (2) (role-holder, gated since T-0738) and clause (3) (owner, deactivation-safe since T-0658). A deactivated actor who genuinely acted on an instance in the past still received, during the residual ~300s access-JWT window, 200 + the participant skeleton + the source record's human title (sourceRecord.title is populated regardless of canOpen). Fix: clause (1) now requires the matched identity (actorSlug, or the distinct fallbackSlug) to be a CURRENTLY active choros.employee row, reusing ACTOR_ACTIVE_SQL (src/db/actor-authority-gate.ts) — the SAME named predicate clause (2) already carries, not a bespoke deactivation literal. Applied to BOTH isInstanceParticipant (single-instance DETAIL path, one point lookup on the matched identity) and isInstanceParticipantBatch (batched LIST path, T-0723's separate sibling — actor-level active status resolved ONCE per page, same as clauses (2)/(3), not per instance). Both functions are new AUTHORITY_RESOLVERS entries in ci/checks/actor-authority-deactivation-gate.sh (they now perform a direct employee slug lookup in process-projection.ts, previously zero) and in the mirrored doc registry in actor-authority-gate.ts (entries H/I).

security_notes: Clause (1) (audit-actor match) now denies unless the matched identity's choros.employee row currently has deactivated_at IS NULL — reusing ACTOR_ACTIVE_SQL verbatim, the SAME literal clause (2) already carries via getRoleSlugsForActor (T-0738). No new deactivation predicate text was introduced.

Fail-closed: a DB error in the new active-check denies clause (1) (never grants), matching the fail-closed posture of every other resolver in this module (clauses (2)/(3), and isInstanceParticipant's overall try/catch discipline).

isInstanceParticipantBatch's active-check is resolved ONCE per LIST page (actor-level, like clauses (2)/(3)), not once per instance — no N+1 introduced; only queried at all when the batch's audit rows carry any actor data (mirrors the existing anyRoles guard on clause (2)).

isInstanceParticipant's tested single-instance body and isInstanceParticipantBatch's separate batched body were BOTH touched (this is the one thing T-0723's own 'don't touch isInstanceParticipant to build the batch sibling' discipline did not anticipate — this task's fix is the one change that must land in both, by definition, since the SAME gap existed in both), but only the clause-(1) block in each; clauses (2)/(3) are byte-unchanged in both functions.

Registered as new AUTHORITY_RESOLVERS entries (ci/checks/actor-authority-deactivation-gate.sh) since both functions now perform a direct employee actor slug-lookup in src/http/process-projection.ts — closing the FF-0662-2 accounting-scan gap this change would otherwise have opened.
judge_attack_surface: Try to make a deactivated actorSlug ride a still-active, DISTINCT fallbackSlug that is NOT itself the identity recorded in this instance's audit track — clause (1) requires the SPECIFIC matched identity to be active, not any identity of the caller.

Confirm isInstanceParticipantBatch's new active-check queries run at most twice TOTAL per LIST page (not per record-less instance) — grep the diff for the query call sites (both sit before the per-instanceId loop) and re-run the existing 'no record-bound projections… participant query still runs' instrumented-pool unit test, which still asserts a single confirmed_by audit query.
Confirm clauses (2)/(3) (getRoleSlugsForActor / isGenesisOwnerForTenant calls and their surrounding try/catch) are byte-unchanged in both functions — only the clause-(1) block was touched.

SRP-8 and the two new db-test anti-cases assert the DEACTIVATED actor's response no longer contains the source record's title at all (404 body / absent from LIST), not merely canOpen:false — the whole participant skeleton is gone, matching SRP-2's existing fail-closed posture for non-participants.

Verify the FF-0662-2 accounting scan still catches a hypothetical THIRD un-gated employee slug-lookup added to either function in the future (the registry entry alone is not the anti-recurrence teeth — the accounting scan counting lookups-vs-predicates inside the registered function body is).
friction_events: The fake pool shared by src/__tests__/processes-read-visibility.test.ts routes ANY bare `FROM choros.employee ... slug = $2` query (no role_assignment JOIN) to a single branch — this is the SAME shape getRoleSlugsForActor's own employeeId-resolve query already used (pre-existing, previously routed to an unconditional {rows:[]}, which was harmless only because clause (2)'s SECOND query, the role_assignment JOIN, ALSO always returned [] in this fixture, making the whole role clause a no-op regardless). Adding the new clause-(1) active-check to the SAME shape required updating that shared branch (and two custom inline 'tracking pool' definitions) to answer 'active' by default and 'deactivated' only for slugs listed in a new opts.deactivatedSlugs — otherwise every pre-existing participant-via-audit-actor test in the file would have flipped to 404, since none of their actors were ever an employee row in the fake pool's world before this task.

Two db-test fixtures (processes-read-visibility.db.test.ts's T-0723 'actor who STARTED the record-less instance' DETAIL and LIST tests) used arbitrary unseeded starter slugs as the acting employee — never an actual choros.employee row. Clause (1) never checked employee existence before this task, so it worked; the new active-check requires a real row, so both fixtures now seed the starter via seedEmployee before asserting participant status.
